Brewery means a facility where malt beverages are manufactured that produces more than ten thousand (10,000) barrels (or the equivalent) per year of malt beverages.
Brewpub means any eating establishment in which malt beverages are manufactured on premises, subject to the barrel production limitation prescribed in section 4-63, and are offered for sale to wholesalers; or to consumers for consumption on the premises along with the sale of food; or by the package for consumption off the premises. A brewpub is also authorized to sell distilled spirits, malt beverages, or wines, and which derives at least fifty (50) percent of its total annual gross food and beverage sales from the sale of prepared meals or food; provided, however, that when determining the total annual gross food and beverage sales, barrels of malt beverages sold to licensed wholesale dealers or to the public for consumption off the premises, shall not be used.
Broker means any person who purchases or obtains an alcoholic beverage from an importer, distillery, brewery, or winery and sells the alcoholic beverage to another broker, importer, or wholesaler without having custody of the alcoholic beverage or maintaining a stock of the alcoholic beverage.
Business means any person, corporation, partnership, or other legal entity which exerts substantial efforts within the city, engages in, causes to be engaged in, and/or represents or holds out to the public to be engaged in any occupation or activity with the object of gain or benefit, either directly or indirectly.
Brown-bagging or BYOB means the possession of, or bringing, taking, or carrying, of any alcoholic beverage into any business licensed to operate within the City of Cairo, or at a location different from where said alcoholic beverage was purchased; provided that bringing an alcoholic beverage into a house, apartment, room or other unit designated for private residential occupancy, or that shall be operated by a not for profit organization, shall not fall within this definition.
Case means a box or receptacle containing not more than two hundred eighty-eight (288) ounces of malt beverages on the average.
Caterer of food means any person who prepares food for consumption off its premises.
Caterer of licensed alcoholic beverages means any retail alcohol dealer licensed by the State of Georgia and holding a license from a Georgia county or municipality to sell or dispense alcoholic beverages. An off-premises special event permit may also be required to sell alcoholic beverages in connection with an authorized catered function.
Church means a body of communicants gathered into church order: united under one (1) form of government by the profession of the same faith and the observance of the same ritual and ceremonies, place where persons regularly assemble in a facility for worship, congregation, or organization for religious purposes.
City special event means an event, held on designated city property, which may include streets and rights-of-way located in the city's downtown business district or a special entertainment district that is organized and sponsored by the City of Cairo or the downtown development authority (DDA), consistent with the provisions of section 4-161 and other applicable provisions of this chapter.
College campus means a collection of two (2) or more buildings used for educational purposes, on either one (1) parcel or contiguous parcels that are under the same ownership by either a public or private institution of higher learning.
Distilled spirits or liquor means any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation or containing more than twenty-four (24) percent alcohol by volume.
Distiller means a manufacturer of distilled spirits.
Establishment means any physical location or section thereof for the operation of a business.
Farm winery means a winery which makes at least forty (40) percent of its annual production from agricultural produce grown in the state where the winery is located.
Food caterer means any person, or individual, company, corporation, association, partnership or other legal entity, who prepares food for consumption off the premises.
Fortified wine, classed as liquor, means any wines or other beverages made by fermentation to which there has been added distilled spirits, and where the alcohol content is more than twenty-one (21) percent alcohol by volume. "Fortified wine" includes, but is not limited to, brandy.
Fruit grower means any person who grows peaches, apples, pears, grapes, or other perishable fruits in this state and who manufactures distilled spirits from the perishable fruits grown in this state.
Gallon or wine gallon means a United States gallon of liquid measure equivalent to the volume of two hundred thirty-one (231) cubic inches or the nearest equivalent metric measurement.
Georgia farm winery means a farm winery which is licensed by the state to manufacture wine in Georgia.
Governing authority means the mayor and council of the City of Cairo.
Growler means a reusable, resealable, and professionally sanitized glass jug used to transport malt beverages or wine for off-premises consumption that is not to exceed sixty-four (64) ounces, and that is filled with malt beverages or wine from a keg by a licensee, or an employee of a licensee, with a malt beverage and/or wine license for consumption off premises issued by the City of Cairo, and purchased by a licensee from a duly licensed wholesaler.
Hard cider means an alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of the juice of apples, containing not more than six (6) percent alcohol by volume, including, but not limited to, flavored or carbonated cider. For purposes of this chapter, hard cider shall be deemed a malt beverage. The term does not include "sweet cider."
Home brewed malt beverage, for purposes of this chapter, shall be limited to malt beverages produced by an individual(s) pursuant to the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 3-5-4.
Hotel or motel, fifty-room, shall mean that business establishment containing a minimum of fifty (50) guest rooms for transient occupancy and constructed to normal size and condition for the hotel or motel industry.
Housing authority means any property containing three hundred (300) housing units or fewer, which property is owned or operated by a housing authority created by article 1 of chapter 3 of title 8 of the Housing Authorities Law.
Importer means any person who imports an alcoholic beverage into this state from a foreign country and sells the alcoholic beverage to another importer, broker or wholesaler and who warehouses a stock of the alcoholic beverage.
Legal age, as used in this chapter, is identical with the legal age provided in the acts of the legislature of the State of Georgia relative to alcoholic beverages and as the same may from time to time be amended.
License shall mean the authorization by the governing authority of the City of Cairo to engage in the sale of alcoholic beverages.
Licensee means any person who holds a license from the city to engage in the selling, manufacturing, distributing or importing at retail or wholesale, of any alcoholic beverages.
Lounge means a separate room connected with a part of, and adjacent to, a restaurant with all booths, stools, and tables being unobstructed and open to view. All lounges shall be air conditioned and have a seating capacity of at least forty (40).
Malt beverage or beer means any alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of any infusion or decoction of barley, malt, hops, or any other similar product, or any combination of such products in water, containing not more than fourteen (14) percent alcohol by volume, and including ale, porter, brown, stout, lager beer, small beer and strong beer. The term "malt beverage" does not include sake, known as Japanese rice wine.
Manufacture means to produce or bottle malt beverages/beer, wine, or distilled spirits/liquor.
Manufacturer means:
(1) In the case of distilled spirits, any person engaged in distilling, rectifying, or blending any distilled spirits;
(2) In the case of malt beverages, any brewer; and
(3) In the case of wine, any vintner; provided, however, that a vintner that blends wine with distilled spirits to produce a fortified wine shall not be considered a manufacturer of distilled spirits.
Minor means any person less than twenty-one (21) years of age.
Nonprofit, charitable and civic organization, means a bona fide nonprofit civic organization which is exempt from Federal Income Tax pursuant to the provisions of subsection (c), (d), or (e) of 26 U.S.C. Section 501 of the Internal Revenue Code, as amended.
Open-air cafe means a premises located within a pedestrian court area and adjacent sidewalk of a restaurant where food is available for purchase during all hours of operation and where alcoholic beverages may be purchased from a restaurant facility for consumption within the open-air cafe.
Package means a bottle, can, keg, barrel, or other original consumer container.
Person means any individual, firm, partnership, cooperative, nonprofit membership corporation, social club, joint venture, association, company, corporation, limited liability company, limited liability partnerships, agency, syndicate, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, fiduciary or other group or combination acting as a unit, body politic, or political subdivision, the plural as well as the singular member, whether public, private, or quasi-public.
Premises means one (1) physically identifiable place of business operated by the same ownership and overall management consisting of one (1) or more contiguous rooms with only one (1) address registered as a single place of business. "Premises" is further defined to include the following areas:
(1) In the case of hotels or motels of fifty (50) rooms, or private clubs, the boundary lines, as well as the swimming pool which is owned by said hotel, motel or club.
(2) Outdoor areas or patios approved pursuant to this chapter.
(3) In the case of a malt beverage and/or wine licensee where a golf course is located adjacent to and contiguous with a restaurant, the playing area of the golf course.
(4) In the case of an open-air cafe, the pedestrian court area and sidewalk in front of the building in which the restaurant is contained.
Private club, bona fide, means any nonprofit association organized under the laws of this state which:
(1) Has been in existence at least one (1) year prior to the filing of its application for a license to be issued pursuant to this chapter;
(2) Has at least seventy-five (75) regular dues-paying members;
(3) Owns, hires or leases a building or space within a building for the reasonable use of its members, which building or space:
a. Has suitable kitchen and dining room space and equipment; and
b. Is staffed with a sufficient number of employees for cooking, preparing and serving meals for its members and guests; and
(4) Has no member, officer, agent or employee directly or indirectly receiving, in the form of salary or other compensation, any profits from the sale of alcoholic beverages beyond a fixed salary.
Private function means any affair where attendance is by invitation only, where no business transactions are conducted during the private function and there is no cost to attend or to consume the food or alcohol either by donations or by any other means. Exception: Should there be an entrance fee or ticket purchase required, an alcohol license and event permit is also required.
Private residence means a house, dwelling or building wherein not less than one (1) family customarily resides. This shall not apply to any of the above which has been unoccupied for a period of twelve (12) consecutive months immediately prior to the filing of an application hereunder.
Resident means a person whose primary residence is within the territorial limits of the city.
Restaurant or eating establishment means any public place kept, used, maintained, advertised and held out to the public as a place where meals are actually and regularly prepared and served, such place being provided with adequate and sanitary kitchen and dining room equipment, air conditioned, having employed therein a sufficient number and kind of employees to prepare, cook and serve suitable food for its guests for every hour they are open. At least one (1) meal per day shall be served at least five (5) days a week, except that restaurants that open for business more than five (5) days a week, shall be required to serve at least one (1) meal per day each day that the restaurant is open, with the exception of holidays, vacation and periods of redecoration, and the serving of such meals shall be the principal business conducted, with the serving of alcoholic beverages to be consumed on the premises as only incidental thereto.
Retail consumption dealer means any person who sells alcoholic beverages at retail for consumption on the premises only to consumers and not for resale.
Retail package dealer means any person who sells alcoholic beverages, in unbroken packages, at retail, intended for carry-out, only to consumers and not for resale.
Retail package distilled spirits/liquor store means a retail business establishment owned by an individual, partnership, corporation, association, or other business entity which is primarily engaged in the retail sale of distilled spirits, malt beverages, and wine in unbroken packages, not for consumption on the premises, except as authorized under this chapter.
Retail tobacco store means a commercial establishment where the primary business is the sale of tobacco products and accessories, emphasizing product variety, storage quality (like humidors for cigars), and expertise about products, to include cigar bars.
School shall mean only such state, county, city or other schools as teach the subjects commonly taught in the common schools of this state and shall not include private schools where only specialized subjects such as law, stenography, business, music, art, medicine, dentistry, vocational occupations and other special subjects are taught.
Sidewalk cafe means an area in front of a restaurant, as defined by projecting its interior width outward perpendicular to the street to a point at which it intersects the roadway, or within the sidewalk frontage of the building where the licensed restaurant is located) and used by a restaurant for additional seating.
Special entertainment district means an area designated by the city council where alcohol can be sold and then consumed on the streets and sidewalks within the clearly-marked bounds of the district.
Standard case means six (6) containers of 1.75 liters, twelve (12) containers of seven hundred fifty (750) milliliters, twelve (12) containers of one (1) liter, twenty-four (24) containers of five hundred (500) milliliters, twenty-four (24) containers of three hundred seventy-five (375) milliliters, forty-eight (48) containers of two hundred (200) milliliters, or one hundred twenty (120) containers of fifty (50) milliliters.
Tasting room means an outlet for the promotion of a manufacturer's product by providing samples of such product to the public on the premises where manufactured, or on premises adjacent thereto under common ownership, and for the sale of such product at retail for consumption on the premises and for sale in closed packages for consumption off the premises. Samples can be given free of charge or for a fee. Offsite tasting rooms of a domestic farm winery may only be located within a special entertainment district designated by the council.
Vintner means one (1) who blends wine with distilled spirits to produce a fortified wine.
Wholesaler or wholesale dealer means any person who sells alcoholic beverages to other wholesale dealers, to retail package dealers, or to retail consumption dealers.
Wine means any alcoholic beverage containing not more than twenty-one (21) percent alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries, or grapes either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. "Wine" includes, but is not limited to, all sparkling wines, champagnes, combinations of such beverages, vermouths, special natural wines, rectified wines, and like products. The term "wine" does not include cooking wine mixed with salt or other ingredients so as to render it unfit for human consumption as a beverage. A liquid shall first be deemed to be a wine at the point in the manufacturing process when it conforms to the definition of wine contained in this section.
Wine, fortified, classed as distilled spirits/liquor, means any alcoholic beverage containing more than twenty-one (21) percent alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries, or grapes either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term includes, but is not limited to, brandy.
Wine tasting means an event as defined in the rules and regulations of the Georgia Department of Revenue and approved by a permit issued by the city.
Winery means a place for the manufacture of wine.
Winery, farm winery means a winery which makes at least forty (40) percent of its annual production from agricultural produce grown in the state.
Winery, Georgia farm, means a farm winery which is licensed by the state to manufacture wine in Georgia.

145:
It shall be unlawful for any person to sell or offer for sale at wholesale or retail any alcoholic beverages, as defined in section 4-2, which shall include malt beverages/beer, wine, and distilled spirits, within the city without having first complied with the provisions of this chapter.

146:
(a) No person shall manufacture, distribute, sell, handle, or possess for sale, or otherwise deal in, alcoholic beverages without first obtaining all applicable licenses or permits required by this chapter.
(b) Each original application provided for in this chapter shall be considered and passed upon by the mayor and council in regular or special session, legally assembled. Upon approval of the application and payment of the required license fee, the applicant shall be entitled to the issuance of the license; provided, however, the mayor and council reserve the right to approve such issuance of the license or licenses conditioned upon full and final compliance by the licensee with all applicable city ordinances.
(c) The license fees as required in section 4-12 of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Cairo are due and payable upon approval of the application or by commencement of business.
(d) The city license issued shall be valid for the license year indicated thereon and shall expire at midnight on the last day of March and is due and payable by April 1 of each year thereafter.
(e) Each person holding a license or permit pursuant to this chapter shall display the license or permit prominently at all times on the premises for which it is issued.
(f) A separate license shall be required for each place of business.

147:
(a) To qualify for an alcoholic beverage license, an applicant shall meet the following:
(1) Designate a "managing agent", who may also be the applicant or owner of the business, who meets the defined qualifications in section 4-2. In the case of a nonprofit private club, the managing agent may be an officer of the organization in lieu of a full-time employee if the individual is otherwise qualified.
(2) A licensee for the sale of beer and wine at retail must be a citizen or legal resident alien of the United States possessing authority to own a business, or if the applicant is not a resident of the City of Cairo, the applicant must designate a resident of Cairo as "designated agent" who shall be responsible for any matter relating to the license. All licensed establishments must have and continuously maintain in Cairo a "designated agent" upon whom any process, notice or demand required or permitted by law or under this chapter to be served upon the licensee or owner, may be served. The licensee shall file the name of such agent, along with the written, notarized consent of such agent with the city in such form as may be prescribed. Residency by an applicant within the city issuing the permit or license for beer and wine shall not be a requirement by the city if the applicant designates a resident of the city who shall be responsible for any matter relating to the license.
(3) Have a certificate of occupancy that has been issued by the city for the premises for which an alcoholic beverage license is sought.
(4) A certificate of residency is required for a licensee of a retail distilled spirits package store certifying that the applicant has been a bona fide resident of the city.
(b) Where the application is made on behalf of a corporation, partnership, a limited liability corporation, limited liability partnership, or sole proprietorship, the license shall be issued jointly to the organization and an individual that meets the qualifications of a managing or designated agent.

149:
(a) Distilled spirits/liquor—Package sales. All applications for license made on forms provided by the city clerk, whether original or for renewal, must be accompanied by a full and complete statement under oath of information relative to any and all interests, as hereinbefore defined in this section, in retail liquor package stores. This shall include the names and addresses of all persons with interest in the ownership of the business of selling packaged liquor at retail, together with any interest each person or members of his family has in any other retail liquor store; the ownership of the land and building where such retail business is operated; the amount of rental paid for said land and building and the manner in which the same is determined and to whom and at what intervals it is paid; the name and address (by affidavit from owner, lessor or sub-lessor of such land and building) of all persons having any whole, partial, beneficial or any other interest in and to the land and building on and in which said retail liquor store is to be located; a copy of the proposed lease, and any other information requested by the police department or the mayor and council pertinent to the application under investigation.
(1) Limitation on number of licenses within a family and/or corporation.
a. No person and/or member of his family and/or corporation shall own, hold or control any interest whatsoever in more than one (1) package store license in the City of Cairo to engage in the business of selling liquor by the package at retail.
b. As used in this paragraph, an interest in the license shall be deemed to exist if the person involved is the outright owner of the license, a co-owner of a license, a general or limited partner in a partnership which owns all or any part of a license, a stockholder in any corporation which owns all or any part of a license, an owner or leasing any real estate which is occupied by a retail liquor store, or shares in any income or corpus of any trust fund or estate having any interest in a retail liquor store.
(2) Citizenship, residence requirement.
a. No license for the retail sale of liquor by the package shall be granted to any applicant who has not resided continuously within the State of Georgia for a period of twelve (12) months next preceding the date on which the application is made, except that the wholesalers or distillers are exempt from this residency provision. A licensee that sells packaged liquor must remain a resident of the State of Georgia during the tenure of their license.
(3) No license shall be issued for a new liquor package store, or for the relocation of an existing liquor store, to be located within five hundred (500) yards of any other business licensed to sell package liquor.
(4) Conducting a public hearing on original application.
a. No original application for a license hereunder shall be acted upon or issued by the mayor and council until after advertisement and public hearing thereon, as required in subsection (a)(5) of this Code section.
b. A public hearing upon all original and completed applications for a license hereunder shall be called by the mayor and council for a regular meeting not more than sixty (60) days after the filing of the application.
(5) Advertisement of notice to secure a retail package dealer's license for sale of distilled spirits by the package; signs posted.
a. All applicants for original licenses hereunder shall give notice of the purpose of making such application by advertisement, at least once during the thirty (30) days immediately preceding the date of a public hearing to be held by the mayor and council, in the newspaper which publishes the legal advertisements of the city. Such notice shall be in large boldface type and shall contain the location of the proposed business and shall give the name of the applicant, and if a partnership, the names of the partners, and if a corporation, the names of the officers, and the date and time the mayor and council would hear the application. It shall be the responsibility of the applicant for an original license to advertise the notice of hearing required as follows:
"Notice of application for retail license for distilled spirits/liquor package.
The undersigned has made application to the Mayor and Council of the City of Cairo for a retail license for package distilled spirits/liquor at _______. This application will be heard by the Mayor and Council at its meeting to be held at ___ o'clock p.m. on the ___ day of _______, 20___. /s/ ___________ Owner(s); ___________ Address of Owner(s)".
b. The applicant shall cause to be placed upon the location of the proposed business at least a week prior to the date of hearing, a sign or signs stating the following:
1. "PACKAGE DISTILLED SPIRITS/LIQUOR LICENSE APPLIED FOR. HEARING BEFORE THE MAYOR AND COUNCIL FOR THE CITY OF CAIRO, GEORGIA, AT ___ O'CLOCK P.M. ON THE ___ DAY OF _______, 20___."
2. The sign or signs required by subsection (2) shall be not less that twenty-four (24) inches by thirty-six (36) inches and shall face toward all public streets, alleys, sidewalks or other public property adjoining the proposed location. Such signs shall be placed where they can be easily seen from all public properties adjoining the proposed location.
(6) Each applicant for an original license shall submit a plot plan and floor plan prepared by an architect, engineer, contractor, surveyor or other qualified person showing all compliance with all requirements contained in this section.
(7) Minimum requirements; floor space of retail outlet, parking required, adequate refuse storage required, visibility from exterior.
a. Any structure housing a licensed retail package store, or proposed therefor, under the terms of this section, shall contain not less than one thousand (1,000) square feet of floor space, including customer service and display area, storage area and service areas.
b. Adequate parking shall be provided as defined elsewhere in this Code. Adequate refuse storage space shall be provided with access for servicing by refuse collection vehicles.
c. The store so occupied for retail sales shall be constructed so that three (3) entire outside walls can be seen from the exterior, and visibility, as defined elsewhere in this section, must be provided from the exterior into the customer service and display area. Visibility, as required, may not be blocked by any signs, vending machines, displays or other obstructions.
(8) Completion of proposed licensed premises. Where a building in which a retailer proposes to operate under the provisions of this section is, at the time of application for such license, not in existence, or not yet completed, a license may be approved for such location provided the plans and specifications for the proposed building are filed with the city clerk of Cairo and show clearly a compliance with the other provisions of this section and applicable ordinances of the city. No license shall then be issued and no sales shall be allowed in such establishment until it has been completed in accordance with all other provisions of this section and other applicable ordinances of the city.
(9) Acceptance and consideration of application after rejection. When any license or permit to operate a retail package store under this section is rejected by the mayor and council, the city clerk shall not accept, and the mayor and council shall not consider, any application from the applicant for a license within twelve (12) months from the time of such rejection by the mayor and council.
(10) Time limit for commencement of business in licensed establishments; forfeiture for non-use. Any holder of a license hereunder who shall begin the operation of the business authorized in the license, but who shall for a period of six (6) consecutive months thereafter cease to operate the business as authorized in said license, shall, upon expiration of such six-month period, automatically forfeit such license, which license shall by virtue of such failure to operate, be cancelled without the necessity of any further action of the mayor and council and no refund of license fee shall be made to the license holder; provided, however, that a license holder may apply to the mayor and council to cease business operations for an illness, or other such reasons as the mayor and council in its discretion may approve.
(b) Distilled spirits—Consumption on premises.
(1) A public hearing upon all original and completed applications for a license hereunder shall be called by the mayor and council for a regular meeting not more than sixty (60) days after the filing of the application.
(2) No original application for a license hereunder shall be acted upon or issued by the mayor and council until after advertisement and public hearing thereon, as required in this section.
(3) Advertisement of notice to secure a retail package dealer's license for consumption of distilled spirits on the premises; signs posted.
a. All applicants for original licenses hereunder shall give notice of the purpose of making such application by advertisement, at least once during the thirty (30) days immediately preceding the date of a public hearing to be held by the mayor and council, in the newspaper which publishes the legal advertisements of the city. Such notice shall be in large boldface type and shall contain the location of the proposed business and shall give the name of the applicant, and if a partnership, the names of the partners, and if a corporation, the names of the officers, and the date and time the mayor and council would hear the application. It shall be the responsibility of the applicant for an original license to advertise the notice of hearing required as follows:
"Notice of application for retail license for distilled spirits/liquor consumption on the premises (mixed drinks). The undersigned has made application to the Mayor and Council of the City of Cairo for a retail license for consumption of distilled spirits (liquor) at _______. This application will be heard by the Mayor and Council at 6:00 p.m. on _______, 20___. /s/___________ Owner(s); Address of Owner(s):___________."
b. The applicant shall cause to be placed upon the location of the proposed business at least a week prior to the date of hearing, a sign or signs stating the following:
"DISTILLED SPIRITS/LIQUOR CONSUMPTION ON THE PREMISES LICENSE APPLIED FOR. HEARING BEFORE THE MAYOR AND COUNCIL FOR THE CITY OF CAIRO, GEORGIA WILL BE HELD AT 6:00 P.M. ON THE ___ DAY OF _______, 20___."
c. The sign or signs required by subsection (4)(b)[(a)(5)b.] shall be not less that twenty-four (24) inches by thirty-six (36) inches and shall face toward all public streets, alleys, sidewalks or other public property adjoining the proposed location. Such signs shall be placed where they can be easily seen from all public properties adjoining the proposed location.
(4) General requirements of business licensed hereunder. No application for any license hereunder shall be granted unless the following conditions are met:
a. Licenses shall be granted only to private clubs, non-profit organizations with facilities, restaurants which may include lounges operated in conjunction with such restaurants, and hotels of fifty (50) or more guest rooms.
b. All restaurants applying for or having pouring licenses must, in addition to all other requirements relating to the sale of alcoholic beverages by the drink, meet and maintain the following requirements:
1. Meet all health and sanitation requirements set forth for food service establishments by the city, state and federal government.
2. Must have installed and operative cooking facilities and kitchen equipment for accommodating the demands of sixty (60) food customers.
3. Must have a complete place setting of metal cutlery and non-disposable dishes in regular use for each of sixty (60) food customers.
4. Must have seating, at booths or tables designed for food service, sufficient for at least sixty (60) persons, and such booths or tables shall be large enough to accommodate at least two (2) place settings of metal cutlery and non-disposable dishes.
5. Such a restaurant as contemplated by this section shall be, at all times during the hours hereinafter set forth, prepared to serve full-course meals with a substantial variety of culinary choices, or substantial substitutes therefor, and shall print and maintain a complete menu of same and furnish such printed menu to each food customer, with prices which are competitive with other restaurants within the city, whether or not those restaurants engage in the business of pouring mixed drinks.
6. Foods listed on the required printed menu, or substantial substitutes therefor, must be available from 11:00 a.m., until 9:00 p.m., or if all sales of mixed drinks are stopped before 9:00 p.m., then from 11:00 a.m., until such earlier time as all mixed drink sales have ceased, at least five (5) days a week, with the exception of holidays, vacations, and periods of redecorating. The hours for service of food may be prolonged, but in no event shall mixed drinks be sold at any hour contrary to this chapter.
7. Restaurants shall maintain at least fifty (50) percent of their business volume from the sale of food, private clubs exempted. Food sales shall include all consumable items sold on the premises except alcoholic beverages.
8. In the event food sales fall below fifty (50) percent of the business volume of the licensee for any two (2) consecutive quarters, then the city manager shall request a hearing for the suspension or revocation of such license in accordance with regulation of this chapter. Nothing herein provided shall prevent the chief of police from suspending or revoking such license for any other violations of this chapter.
9. The gross square footage of the dining area, lounge area, serving area, kitchen, restrooms, and storage rooms of any restaurant business other than private clubs, licensed hereunder must be a minimum of two thousand (2,000) square feet. Parking requirements for restaurants licensed hereunder shall be the same as those required in the present ordinances of the city, except that existing restaurants and nonconforming structures will be exempt from such requirements.
10. Completion of proposed licensed premises. Where a building in which a retailer intends to operate under the provisions of this section is at the time of the application for such license not in existence or not yet completed, a license may be issued for such location provided the plans for the proposed building show clearly a compliance with the other provisions of this section. No sales or consumption will be allowed in such establishment until it has been completed in accordance with said plans and is in conformity with all other provisions of this section and the city Code.
c. Special qualifications for private clubs. Private clubs, as defined herein, shall furnish along with license applications, a copy of the articles of incorporation from the State of Georgia, if incorporated by the state, and documentation of the valid up-to-date status of its national or state charter from its parent organization, together with documentation of its compliance denoting a tax-exempt status under Section 501 of the U.S. IRS Code. Private clubs whose primary purpose is not categorized by the term or terms "lodge," "fraternal order," or "veterans post," such as private clubs for golf, tennis and other similar recreation are exempt from the above provision which relates to a national or state charter from a parent organization.
d. Each applicant for an original license, except private clubs, shall submit a plot plan and floor plan prepared by an architect, engineer, contractor, surveyor or other qualified person, showing all compliance with all distance, square foot, kitchen arrangement and food serving area table and seating arrangement requirements contained herein.
e. On renewals, the same as the preceding shall be accomplished unless the applicant states in the reapplication that there has been no change in any of the above compliance items.
f. Sale or delivery to unlicensed premises. It shall be unlawful for any licensee hereunder to make deliveries of any alcoholic beverage by the drink beyond the boundaries of the premises covered by the license.
g. Exterior advertisements and media advertising prohibited.
1. No signs of any kind, painted or electric, advertising any brand or price of alcoholic beverages shall be permitted on the exterior, or in the window of any licensed premises. No placard or sign of any kind which is visible from the exterior of the licensed premises shall make reference to the price of liquors sold therein.
2. No outside signs of any kind shall indicate that liquor by the drink is served within the licensed premises except that restaurants may add to the name of the business the words "and Lounge" onto any legal signs or advertising.
h. Coin-operated devices; provisions. 167:
(a) Malt beverage or wine - manufacturer, retail package, and retail consumption dealer distance requirements.
(1) No malt beverage or wine - manufacturer, retail package, or retail consumption dealer shall be located:
a. Within one hundred (100) yards of any school building, school grounds or college campus.
b. Within one hundred (100) yards of any property containing three hundred (300) housing units or fewer, which property is owned or operated by a housing authority created by article 1 of chapter 3 of title 8 of the Housing Authorities Law.
c. Within one hundred (100) yards of an alcoholic treatment center owned and operated by this state or any county or any municipal government.
(2) This subsection shall not apply:
a. To a grocery store licensed for the retail sale of package wine and malt beverages for consumption off the premises, which shall be allowed to sell wine and malt beverages within one hundred (100) yards of any school building, school grounds or college campus. As used in this subparagraph, the term "grocery store" means a retail establishment which has a total retail floor space of at least ten thousand (10,000) square feet of which at least eighty-five (85) percent is reserved for the sale of food and other nonalcoholic items and conducts all of its sales inside the building containing its retail floor space.
b. To hotels of fifty (50) or more guest rooms.
c. To any premises or location where an alcoholic beverage license was issued or approved prior to the effective date of this ordinance [from which this chapter derives], so long as alcoholic beverages are being sold or dispensed in compliance with the other provisions of this chapter.
d. To any premises or location where alcoholic beverages are being sold or dispensed in compliance with the other provisions of this chapter and a school or college campus is built or erected within the minimum distances provided for in this section.
e. To bona fide private clubs owning their own building.
(b) Distilled spirits - manufacturer, retail package, or retail consumption dealer distance requirements.
(1) No distilled spirits - manufacturer, retail package, or retail consumption dealer shall be located:
a. Within one hundred (100) yards of any church building or within two hundred (200) yards of any school building, education building, school grounds or college campus.
b. Within one hundred (100) yards of any property containing three hundred (300) housing units or fewer, which property is owned or operated by a housing authority created by article 1 of chapter 3 of title 8 of the Housing Authorities Law.
c. Within one hundred (100) yards of an alcoholic treatment center owned and operated by this state or any county or municipal government.
d. Within fifty (50) feet of any private residence. The distance for the purpose of this paragraph shall be measured in all directions from the nearest wall enclosing the building where alcoholic beverages are to be sold to the nearest point of any residential property line, except that the provisions of this paragraph shall not apply on residences located adjacent to or in areas of commercially-zoned property.
(2) The distance provided for herein shall not apply:
a. To any premises or location where alcoholic beverages are being sold or dispensed in compliance with the other provisions of this chapter and a school or church is built or erected within the minimum distances provided for in this section.
b. To any premises or location licensed as an importer, so long as the same is allowed by the state; provided, however, no signs or other forms of advertisement shall be placed on or near the licensed premises, which directly or indirectly advertise that alcoholic beverages are stored or warehoused on the premises.
c. To hotels of fifty (50) or more guest rooms.
d. To bona fide private clubs owning their own buildings.
(c) Unless otherwise provided in this chapter, all measurements to determine distances required by this chapter for the issuance of licenses shall be measured in the following manner:
(1) In a straight line from the front door of the structure from which alcoholic beverages are sold or offered for sale;
(2) To the front door of the building of a church, government-owned treatment center, or a retail package store; or
(3) To the nearest property line of the real property being used for school or educational purposes or property that is owned or operated by a housing authority.
(d) If the sale of alcoholic beverages was lawful at a location during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding an application for renewal or a new application for an alcoholic beverage license, the premises shall be grandfathered in regarding any distance requirements as outlined in this chapter.

169:
(a) The following regulations involving minors shall apply:
(1) No licensee, or employee of such licensee, or any person acting on behalf of, or with the knowledge of such licensee, shall give, sell, offer to sell, knowingly, by himself or through another, furnish, cause to be furnished, or offer to furnish any person any alcoholic beverage who is under the lawful drinking age established by Georgia law.
(2) No person under twenty-one (21) years of age shall purchase, drink, or sell or knowingly possess any alcoholic beverage.
(3) No person knowingly or intentionally shall act as an agent to purchase or acquire any alcoholic beverage for or on behalf of a person under twenty-one (21) years of age.
(4) No person under twenty-one (21) years of age shall misrepresent his age, identity or use any false identification for the purpose of purchasing or obtaining any alcoholic beverage.
(5) No licensee, employee of any licensee, or any person acting on behalf of any licensee shall furnish, sell, or give alcoholic beverages to any person on any day or at any time when the sale of same is prohibited by state law or this chapter.
(b) It shall be the affirmative duty of every licensee, or any person acting on behalf of the licensee, to check the proper identification of every person when selling or otherwise furnishing an alcoholic beverage to such person, or to permit, within the licensee's premises, any person in possession of an alcoholic beverage who is under the lawful drinking age established by Georgia law; and the failure to make such request and verification in any case where the person to whom the alcoholic beverage is sold or otherwise furnished is less than the legal age, may be considered by the trier of fact in determining whether the person selling or otherwise furnishing such alcoholic beverage did so knowingly.
(c) For purposes of this chapter, "proper identification" means any document issued by a governmental agency containing a description of the person, such person's photograph, and giving such person's date of birth and includes, without being limited to, a passport, military identification card, driver's license or an identification card authorized under O.C.G.A. § 40-5-100 et seq. "Proper identification" shall not include a birth certificate.
(d) If a driver's license is altered or indicates that such license is falsified, or is not the driver's license of the person presenting it, or that such person is under the age of twenty-one (21) years, the person to whom said license is tendered shall be authorized to either write down the name and address and license number, or to seize the license, and shall immediately thereafter summon a law enforcement officer who shall be authorized to seize the license either at the scene or at such time as the license can be located.
(e) No person shall be convicted under this section if such person has been furnished with proper identification showing that the person who is being furnished alcoholic beverages is of legal age or over.
(f) The prohibition contained in subsection (a) above shall not apply with respect to the sale, purchase or possession of alcoholic beverages for consumption:
(1) For medical purposes pursuant to a prescription of a physician duly authorized to practice medicine in this state.
(2) At a religious ceremony.
(3) In the home of the minor with the consent of said minor's parent or legal guardian.

181:
(a) A manufacturer of malt beverages in a brewpub must follow certain distance requirements for package and consumption sales from churches, schools, housing authorities, alcoholic treatment centers and other specific locations as required by section 4-38 of this chapter.
(b) All measurements to determine distances required by this chapter shall be measured as provided for in section 4-38.
(c) The holder of a brewpub license shall be required to operate an eating establishment that shall be the sole retail outlet for such malt beverages. A brewpub is also authorized to sell distilled spirits, malt beverages, or wines, and which derives at least fifty (50) percent of its total annual gross food and beverage sales from the sale of prepared meals or food; provided, however, that when determining the total annual gross food and beverage sales, barrels of malt beverages sold to licensed wholesale dealers or to the public for consumption off the premises, shall not be used.
(d) No individual shall be permitted to own or operate a brewpub without first obtaining a proper brewpub license to brew and sell its product for consumption on the premises, or to sell its malt beverages by the package for consumption off the premises through its existing brewpub license and is not required to obtain a separate package beer license. A licensee may offer for sale for consumption on or off the premises any other alcoholic beverages produced by other manufacturers which are authorized for retail sale under this Code, including wine, distilled spirits, and other malt beverages; provided that such other alcoholic beverages are purchased from a licensed wholesaler. Licenses for the sale of other alcoholic beverages obtained from a wholesaler shall be required in addition to the brewpub license.
(e) A brewpub license authorizes the holder of such license to:
(1) Manufacture on the licensed premises not more than ten thousand (10,000) barrels of malt beverage in a calendar year solely for retail sale. Brewpubs are also authorized to sell up to five thousand (5,000) barrels of malt beverages manufactured annually to licensed wholesale dealers. Under no circumstances shall such malt beverages be sold by a brewpub licensee to any person holding a retail consumption dealer's license or a retailer's package license for the purpose of resale.
(2) A limited exception to the provisions for the distribution and sale of malt beverages shall exist to the extent that the license to manufacture malt beverages in this state shall include the right to sell malt beverages produced at the brewer's licensed premises to individuals who are on such premises for:
a. Consumption on the premises; and
b. Consumption off the premises, provided that such sales for consumption off the premises shall not exceed a maximum of two hundred eighty-eight (288) ounces (one (1) case) of malt beverages per consumer per day.
(3) A brewpub licensee shall pay all license fees as well as excise taxes as prescribed by section 4-176 applicable to individuals licensed under this Code as manufacturer, retailer, and where applicable, wholesale dealer.
(4) In addition, brewpubs may sell and fill growlers, provided the licensee does not also sell distilled spirits.
(5) Except as set forth in this section, a brewpub licensee shall be subject to all sections of this chapter, and each brewpub licensee shall comply with all other applicable state and local license requirements including the limited sale of malt beverages to the public, and may sell on all days and at all times that sales of malt beverages by retailers are lawful within the city.
